newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico arrests seven members of top drug gang.
newsitem.headline: Mexico arrests seven members of top drug gang.

text.p: Seven former members of Mexico's anti-drug forces who were also on cocaine baron Amado Carrillo Fuentes' payroll have been arrested, officials said on Tuesday.

Police arrested three former federal judicial police agents, three former members of the armed forces and Fernando Graciano Garcia, a former official at the defunct National Institute for Combatting Drugs (INCD).

Officials said the arrests were made after two former military men tried to bribe the head of an army border post in the southern state of Campeche to allow a plane carrying illegal drugs to land safely.
"Faced with such an offer, the man in charge of the military post, acting with a sense of duty and honesty, proceeded to arrest the men," a statement from the attorney general's office said.
"(The arrests are) a heavy blow to the organisation headed by the narco-trafficker Amado Carlos Fuentes, alias the Lord of the Skies," the statement said.
Carrillo Fuentes gained his nickname for his brazen tactic of using commerical aircraft for ferrying drug loads destined for the United States from Colombia to Mexico.
It was not immediately clear what post Graciana had held at the INCD, which was recently scrapped after its head, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, was arrested on charges of drug corruption.

Mexico last month replaced the INCD with a new anti-drug unit called the Special Prosecutor's Office for Crimes Against Health in an effort to clean an image tarnished by the arrest of Gutierrez and other recent drug scandals.
